timeline.title: A Short History of Great Teaching
items: The oldest university
The University of Bologna opened its doors. It is still teaching students today.
A garden of children
Friedrich Froebel opened a school for little ones built on play. He called it a kindergarten.
Learning by doing
Maria Montessori opened her first school in Rome, letting children learn through curious hands.
A day for teachers
UNESCO made 5 October World Teachers' Day, to thank teachers all over the world.
today: Not in the history books yet. But in ours, the best teacher there ever was.

An old Chinese saying
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: thank you, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Learning
items: spark
Growing brains
By around age six, a child's brain is already about ninety percent of its adult size.
key
Mistakes help
Making a mistake and then fixing it is one of the best ways the brain learns something new.
star
Praise for trying
Studies show children praised for effort are more willing to take on hard problems.
moon
Learning in your sleep
Sleep helps the brain store what we learned that day. Bedtime is homework too.
book
Teach to learn
Explaining something to someone else helps you remember it better yourself.
leaf
Children's garden
Kindergarten is German for children's garden: a place where little minds can grow.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It still cannot explain how {who} made every single one of us feel special.

note.title: What we believe a teacher is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe a great teacher is not only lessons and marking. A great teacher is the smile at the door, the patience on a hard morning, and the moment a child realises: I can do this.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not a mug or a card, but pages full of you: your words, your lessons, the little things that made this year magic.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you made a difference that will last a lifetime.
